result.summary: Measurement-first audit of the Founder's reported 3-5s Native cold-load-after-idle. No Founder Production credentials were available, so no live authenticated device trace was obtained (none sought/fabricated). Used real production runtime logs from an actual recent Founder session (Home 2.4s/3.6MB, Log 2.3s/9.2MB, Nutrition/Activity/Energy ~1-1.4s/~4MB each, DB pool waitingCount hit 10 vs pool of 5), full code-level architecture mapping of Native (2bfbf54a) and exact-prod Server (93491bc5), and a local fixture-scale render experiment ruling out client rendering as dominant. Dominant causes: (C) unbounded full-history Server queries with no DB-level pagination, and (E) Native's in-memory-only cache plus an explicit flag disabling iOS's HTTP disk cache, so every cold launch is a guaranteed full miss. Secondary: (A) mandatory post-idle auth refresh plus an unmeasured per-request 5-DB-round-trip auth check; (D) a confirmed cheap-to-fix duplicate-fetch bug (Weight/Nutrition/Activity scope mismatches Evidence Hub/Log). Delivered ranked P0/P1/P2 bottlenecks and a sequenced plan; recommend deferring all fixes to Build 51 (HealthKit Build 50 verified untouched). Audit only, no implementation.

tests.summary: No code changes were made (audit-only task); no test suite was run beyond a local Debug build succeeding for the fixture-scale render measurement.

review.summary: No code changes were made; nothing to review.

zero_write_audit.summary: All production access was read-only (doctl apps get-deployment/apps logs/apps spec get, and unauthenticated curl connection-timing probes returning 401/405 with no data). No Native app was run against Founder Production. No Server code was built for or deployed to production.

decisions_required: Whether to authorize a follow-up pass with a live authenticated on-device trace (requires the Founder to log into Founder Production once on a Debug build in a fresh simulator, or to provide/authorize a bounded test-account token) to replace the fixture-scale render measurement and production-log-based server timing with a true end-to-end device trace.

Whether to fold the single small additive item (promoting NativePerformanceDiagnostics to release builds) into the pending Build 50, or defer everything including that item to Build 51 as recommended.

Authorize the P0 fixes for a Build 51 performance pass: server-side query bounding (Home/Training/Nutrition/Weight/Timeline/Photos), Native persisted-snapshot cache redesign, and the Weight/Nutrition/Activity scope-mismatch fix.

Authorize the low-risk Server ops changes (raise PHYSIQUEOS_DATABASE_POOL_MAX, commit PHYSIQUEOS_PROVIDER_READ_DIAGNOSTICS=1 into the checked-in template) independently of the larger Build 51 work, since they need no Native build at all.
blockers: No Founder Production credentials/authenticated session available in this environment, so a true live on-device cold-launch/idle-resume trace (COLD_LAUNCH_MEASURED / IDLE_RESUME_MEASURED at full fidelity) could not be obtained. Worked around via real production runtime logs plus fixture-scale local rendering, but this is a real gap versus the task's ideal method — flagged rather than silently worked around.
unexpected_findings: PHYSIQUEOS_PROVIDER_READ_DIAGNOSTICS=1 is set in the live deployed App Platform spec but not in the checked-in infra/digitalocean/*.yaml templates -- a redeploy-from-template would silently lose the per-query diagnostics this audit relied on.

A concrete, narrow, cheap-to-fix duplicate-fetch bug: Weight/Nutrition/Activity screens default to context=build-lean-mass while Evidence Hub and Log use context=all, so drilling from Evidence Hub into any of those three screens is a guaranteed cache-miss re-fetch of data just displayed seconds earlier.

The Native client explicitly sets request.cachePolicy = .reloadIgnoringLocalCacheData on every request, which disables iOS's own free HTTP disk cache on top of the custom in-memory cache being empty on every cold launch -- there is no caching fallback at any layer for a freshly launched process.

The primary Server bulk-read path (NativeProductionContractService.read(), backing every page in this audit) has zero success-path latency logging; the rich per-query diagnostics that produced this report's numbers exist only via the undocumented live spec env-var override noted above.

DB connection pool is fixed at the default of 5 and was observed queuing for real (waitingCount reaching 10) under Evidence Hub's own 7-concurrent-GET fan-out -- a real, currently-live concurrency bottleneck, not a hypothetical one.
'Home priority navigation' as a specifically named prior feature/incident was not found in the codebase or git history under that name; closest candidates identified and flagged rather than guessed.
backlog: Build 51 performance pass: bound unbounded full-history Server queries (Home/Training/Nutrition/Weight/Timeline/Photos) with real SQL-level LIMIT/date-window filtering
Build 51 performance pass: Native persisted last-known-snapshot cache with explicit freshness semantics, replacing the in-memory-only cache and removing the blanket .reloadIgnoringLocalCacheData
Native fix: align Weight/Nutrition/Activity default query scope with Evidence Hub/Log's context=all to eliminate the confirmed duplicate-fetch path
Server ops: raise PHYSIQUEOS_DATABASE_POOL_MAX and commit PHYSIQUEOS_PROVIDER_READ_DIAGNOSTICS=1 into the checked-in app-spec template
Server: short-TTL cache for per-request auth-token validation and for the canonical exercise registry lookup
Native: promote NativePerformanceDiagnostics (network/decode/shell timing) from #if DEBUG to a redacted, rate-limited release build metric
Follow-up task: live authenticated on-device cold-launch/idle-resume trace once Founder credentials/test-account access is arranged
recommended_next_step: Decide whether to authorize a live authenticated on-device follow-up trace, then sequence the Build 51 performance work per the report's optimization plan starting with the zero-code Server ops changes (DB pool size, diagnostics env var) and the small Native scope-mismatch fix, both independently low-risk and not blocked on anything else.
